definition: Generating images as next-token prediction over discrete visual tokens from a VQ tokenizer, the pre-diffusion paradigm revived by unified any-to-any models that emit text and image tokens from one transformer.
details: Generating images as next-token prediction over discrete visual tokens from a VQ tokenizer, the pre-diffusion paradigm revived by unified any-to-any models that emit text and image tokens from one transformer. The architectural bet that one autoregressive backbone can own all modalities.

explainer.lead: Autoregressive image generation creates a picture one discrete visual token at a time, with each prediction conditioned on the tokens already produced. It matters because the same next-token transformer used for text can also emit images, allowing one backbone to handle multiple modalities.

tiers.eli5: Imagine making a picture from a set of tiny puzzle pieces, choosing one piece at a time while looking at all the pieces you have already placed. A special codebook turns pictures into pieces a computer can predict, then turns the finished sequence back into a picture. This lets the same kind of machine that writes words one by one also make images one piece at a time.
tiers.practitioner: Encode training images into discrete codes with a VQ tokenizer, then train a transformer to predict each code from its predecessors, optionally conditioning on text tokens. At inference, sample or otherwise select codes sequentially and pass the completed sequence to the VQ decoder. A unified any-to-any setup places text and image tokens in the same transformer workflow; image codes still need decoding rather than being interpreted as pixels.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a VQ-encoded image x = (x_1, ..., x_T), autoregressive generation factorizes its distribution as p(x) = product over t of p(x_t | x_1, ..., x_(t-1)); text or other tokens can be added as conditioning context. The transformer operates over the discrete visual representation, and the resulting codes are decoded into an image.

explainer.example: Given the prompt “a red apple on a table,” a unified model first reads the text tokens, then predicts illustrative visual codes such as 42, 17, 9, and 5 in order. Each prediction can attend to the prompt and earlier codes, and the VQ decoder turns the finished code sequence into the apple image.

usedIn.name: Unified any-to-any models
usedIn.detail: A single transformer can emit text tokens and image tokens, sharing one autoregressive backbone across modalities.

usedIn.name: Image generation
usedIn.detail: Pictures are produced as sequences of discrete visual codes and then reconstructed with a VQ decoder.

explainer.intuition: Treat an image less like a canvas to be painted all at once and more like a sentence to be continued. Once a VQ tokenizer gives the image a discrete vocabulary, the familiar next-token prediction problem can produce pictures as well as text.
howItWorks: Use a VQ tokenizer to represent an image as an ordered sequence of discrete visual tokens.
Train a transformer to predict each visual token from the tokens before it.
For conditional generation, provide text or other modality tokens as context to the same transformer.
Generate the visual sequence token by token, feeding each new token back into the model.
Decode the completed visual tokens with the VQ decoder to obtain the image.
explainer.whyItMatters: It offers a direct way to bring image generation into the next-token framework used for language. The larger architectural bet is that one autoregressive backbone can own all modalities instead of requiring a separate image generator.
misconceptions: It is not diffusion: it predicts discrete tokens sequentially rather than generating through a denoising process.
The model does not have to predict raw pixels; the tokens come from a VQ tokenizer.
Autoregressive image generation does not require a unified text-and-image model, although that is one important use.
